subject: SIG: allowlist & VPC peering evidence — Zenith Health request
messages:
From: Anya Kozlova <anya.kozlova@zenithhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: SIG: Network evidence request — VPC peering & private endpoints

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this. As part of Zenith Health's SIG review we need a focused network evidence pack for the Redwood deployment that will be handling PHI-adjacent traffic. Can you provide the following items?

- Canonical list of public egress IP ranges we can allowlist for outbound traffic (by region).
- Diagram showing VPC peering/private endpoint topology used for the Redwood Private deployment (PNG/SVG).
- Proof of private endpoint configuration (screenshots or console export) and the DNS entries customers should use.
- Security group / firewall rule exports showing allowed ports for the service.
- A single zipped evidence package (preferable) or a drive link if files are large.

Timebox: our security team would like something by EOD Thursday PDT (2027-08-05). Is that feasible? Also please indicate any items that require an NDA or additional intake.

Best,
Anya
Senior Security Engineer, Zenith Health
security@zenithhealth.com

--
Zenith Health | 1-888-ZEN-HEAL

Subject: Re: SIG: Network evidence request — VPC peering & private endpoints

Hi Anya — thanks for the clear list. We can deliver a consolidated evidence bundle. At a high level we'll provide:

- Egress IP table (CSV) per region + TTL notes for ephemeral pools
- VPC peering / PrivateLink topology diagram (SVG) and short narrative
- Console exports/screenshots for private endpoint configuration and DNS guidance
- Security group / NACL export (CSV) that maps to service ports and protocols
- A single zip containing the above plus a README that maps the files to your SIG questions.

Target delivery: 2027-08-04 EOD PDT. If anything materially blocks that date, I'll escalate. Nothing here requires a new NDA — we can provide redacted console exports.

Two quick asks for your team: 1) confirm the primary Zen-Env (prod vs staging) you want evidence for, and 2) are there additional IPs you expect us to include for partner-originated traffic?

I'll attach the final bundle to this thread and share a Drive link. CC'ing my CS and networking leads to coordinate.

Thanks,
Sooj

Let's target internal draft by EOD Wed (2027-08-03) so we can complete packaging by Thu EOD. Flag any blockers here.

Subject: Re: Internal: Zenith SIG — allowlist/evidence triage (quick)

Quick update — attached exports and notes (referenced filenames below). I captured the current production egress ranges and included a short note about ephemeral NAT pools for Dedicated customers: they rotate on a 7-14 day window unless customer requests a static egress allocation.

Key files I prepared:
- egress-ip-table.csv (region,ip_range,notes)
- security-groups-export.csv (group_id,port_range,protocol,description)
- peering-diagram.svg (diagram showing peering + PrivateLink endpoints)
- console-screenshot-private-endpoint-setup.png (redacted)

Ports/protocols we allow for upstream communication: 443/TCP outbound; health-check 8080/TCP on private side for internal probes (documented). No inbound public ports exposed on the endpoint.

I'll hand the bundle to Marissa for packaging once Hannah confirms SOC2 mappings for references.

—Karthik
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Anya — delivering the evidence bundle and next steps. Attached: zenith_vpc-allowlist.csv, peering-diagram.svg, console-screenshot-private-endpoint-setup.png, security-groups-export.csv, and sig-evidence-bundle.zip. Also sharing a Drive folder with the same artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-zenith-sig-evidence

Summary highlights:
- Egress IPs: see zenith_vpc-allowlist.csv — includes region column and notes on ephemeral NAT TTLs (ephemeral pools typically rotate every 7–14 days unless customer purchases static allocation).
- Topology: peering-diagram.svg shows PrivateLink endpoints and the recommended DNS names to resolve to private endpoints.
- Ports: service uses outbound 443/TCP to upstream and internal probe on 8080/TCP; no inbound public ports on private endpoints.

Next steps: please confirm if you need a signed attestation or additional console recordings. We can schedule a short walkthrough with Karthik if your SOC team wants live verification. If the ring looks good, we'll update the SIG spreadsheet with the specific file references and close this out.

Timeline note: we aimed for Thu EOD — delivered earlier. If you need a different format (e.g., specific CSV column ordering or a JSON manifest), tell us and we'll repackage.

Best regards,
Sooj
